subject: HearthCare Labs — hosting mode selection & recommended serving footprint
messages:
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@hearthcare.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Serving model for regulated PII workflows — initial questions

Hi Evelyn / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Quick follow-up from the product/security side: HearthCare is evaluating whether to run patient-facing inference in Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity in your shared control plane) vs Redwood Private (VPC-hosted control plane and isolated inference nodes).

Key constraints:
- Data residency + PHI handling: must be in our US-only VPC; audit logs retained 7 years.
- Peak inference: expected 700 qps (short bursts) across 4 model endpoints, median prompt length ~350 tokens.
- Latency SLO: 99p token latency < 120ms for standard text generation.
- Cost: procurement needs a forecasted 12-month run-rate for committed capacity.

Can you share opinionated guidance on the fleet footprint (GPU types & counts), estimated token throughput, and tradeoffs (SLA, procurement complexity, infra ops) so we can evaluate costs and legal? Also please attach any standard SOC2 artifact flow for Private installs.

—Jordan
Jordan Price
Director, Product Integrations
HearthCare Labs
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@hearthcare.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Serving model for regulated PII workflows — initial questions

Jordan — thanks for the clear constraints. I pulled together a short write-up (attached) and a conservative serving footprint so procurement has numbers to model. High-level summary up front, details below and in attachments.

Short answer (opinionated):
- Dedicated: faster procurement/launch (we can map to reserved pools), lower operational lift for HearthCare (Redwood manages runtime, telemetry stays in Redwood control plane). Good if HearthCare wants rapid time-to-value and accepts a shared control plane with strict network isolation.
- Private: stricter for compliance (control plane and inference nodes inside your VPC), required if legal needs full tenant control or air-gapped operations. Higher up-front procurement (dedicated server ordering / private networking) and a larger recommended GPU footprint to maintain the same burst SLOs due to reduced multi-tenant multiplexing.

Attached: hcls_hosting_tradeoffs_v1.pdf (2 pages), hcls_estimated_gpu_run_rates.csv (model-by-model throughput). I call out two recommended deployments in the attached sheet (QuickStart Dedicated & VPC Private baseline).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Review the attached baseline numbers with your infra team.
2) If Private is required, we should schedule a 1-hour runbook sync with your cloud/security leads to scope KMS, audit log delivery, and VPC peering.
3) If Dedicated is acceptable, Marissa will send the reserved-capacity quote and a 30-day pilot addendum.

I'll summarize the footprint below per Markus' inputs (copied inline).

—Evelyn

Evelyn / team — pasted below is the engineering-backed estimate. Numbers assume current open-source LLMs with KV caching and 16-bit quantized weights on A100/RTX 6000-equivalent hardware for Dedicated; Private assumes the same model family but we recommend slightly larger headroom due to less cross-tenant multiplexing.

Quoted assumptions (see CSV for per-endpoint detail):
- 4 endpoints, median prompt 350 tokens, median completion 120 tokens (output) -> median request ~470 tokens processed per call.
- Typical batching savings: Dedicated (multi-tenant) = 1.6x batching roll-up during peak windows; Private = 1.25x (less diverse fan-in).
- KV cache hit rate assumption: 18% for Dedicated, 14% for Private (customer workload profile).

Recommended footprints (serving nodes using 80GB GPU equivalents):
- Dedicated (recommended starter): 8 GPUs (80GB class) + 2x warm spare nodes. Estimated steady throughput ~450 qps; peak burst headroom to ~700 qps with autoscale burst (30–45s provision). Estimated 99p token latency: 85–110ms (meets 120ms target under typical traffic).
- Private (compliance-first): 12 GPUs (80GB class) + 4x warm spares (to preserve headroom). Estimated steady throughput ~380 qps; peak burst headroom ~700 qps but requires a larger cold-to-hot instance pool and tuned pre-warming to meet 99p < 120ms consistently.

Cost/ops tradeoffs:
- Dedicated: lower capital ops on customer's side, shorter lead time (3–5 weeks for reservation + config), Redwood manages kernel tuning and tracing.
- Private: longer procurement (4–8 weeks for dedicated infra + network setup), more customer operational responsibility for patching/backups unless you purchase our Private Ops add-on.

Attachments referenced: redwood_dedicated_quote_v2.xlsx contains a 12-month committed cost estimate with both scenarios.

If we want to tighten these numbers I can run a lightweight perf sim (1–2 days) using HearthCare sample traffic to validate batching and KV assumptions.

—Markus

Recommendation: start with Redwood Dedicated as a pilot (8x80GB GPUs + 2 spares) for the 30–60 day pilot. This minimizes procurement friction, gets you to production faster, and lets us validate real batching/KV behaviors against your traffic. If after the pilot HearthCare legal still requires private-control-plane isolation, we’ve included a clear migration runbook and Private baseline footprint (12x80GB + 4 spares) in the attached docs.

- Technical: if you can share a 72-hour sample of production traffic (anonymized), Markus can run the perf sim and give a tightened GPU recommendation within 48 hours.
- Compliance: Neha will share the SOC2 artifact flow and our Private deployment checklist once procurement signals go-ahead (I attached the initial SOC2 pointer in the drive link).

Happy to jump on a 30-min sync next week to walk procurement/legal through the tradeoffs.
